To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the root number of any distinguished pair of cuspidal representations is trivial, that the gamma factor at s = 1/2 of any distinguished cuspidal representation is trivial, that any cuspidal representation with a trivial gamma factor at s=1/2 is distinguished, and that any cuspidall representation with trivial gamma factor at 0 is distinguished.

the local Rankine–Selberg root numbers for any distinguished representations are trivial, and the global root number is trivial for distinguished cuspidal automorphic representations of $G L_{2} \left(\right. A_{K} \left.\right)$, where $K$ is a number field with a quadratic extension.

the local root number of any two distinguished representations is trivial, and the converse holds when the local root number is trivial; the gamma factor of a distinguished representation is trivial when the local root is trivial; and the converse holds in the case of a distinguished representation of a special type.
